nodes.name: Webhook (postevent-demo)
nodes.notes: POST path 'postevent-demo'. responseMode=responseNode -- the actual HTTP response is sent later by one of the two 'Respond:' nodes (success or module-error), not immediately on receipt, because the response body IS the pipeline result.

nodes.name: Normalize Trigger Input
nodes.notes: Same node receives items from both triggers. Manual Trigger emits {} (no 'body' key) so every field falls through to its default; Webhook emits the POST JSON under 'body'. No optional chaining used (kept to plain && checks) to stay conservative about what the n8n 2.35.7 expression sandbox accepts.

nodes.name: Build Run Request
nodes.notes: Assembles the /api/run body. Defaults event_name to the real event this repo targets when the trigger carried nothing. Critically: registrants_csv / transcript_md are only included in base_request when non-empty -- api/run.py's materialize_event() checks `is not None`, so sending '' would count as a caller-supplied (empty) file and break M1/M2/M3, instead of falling back to the bundled fixture as intended. Omitting the key (leaving it undefined) is what triggers the fixture fallback.

nodes.name: Derive Run Key
nodes.notes: Idempotency key = slug(event_name) + execution date (YYYY-MM-DD), deterministic across re-runs of the same event on the same day. This demo lane performs no writes so there is nothing to dedupe here; a production instance would look this key up in a store (Postgres row, n8n Data table, or a HubSpot custom object keyed on event_tag) before letting any write-side node fire, and would write the key back only after a successful run. See notes on 'Merge Module Summaries' for how run_key reaches the response.

nodes.name: Health Check — GET /api/run
nodes.notes: Generic HTTP: the engine's public API has no native n8n node. GET returns {ok, repo_root_ok, live_available, model_chain, modules, error?} per api/run.py's build_get_response() -- ok now equals repo_root_ok (real deployment health), not a hardcoded true; error is only present when repo_root_ok is false. Does not pass ?probe=1 -- that opts into a live OpenRouter ping and this health check should stay free/cheap on every run. onError=continueErrorOutput so a fully-down deployment (DNS/connect/timeout failure) routes to the StopAndError branch below with a legible message instead of the whole execution just red-X'ing with a raw HTTP-node error.

nodes.name: Service Healthy? (ok)
nodes.notes: Gates on ok only, deliberately not on live_available too: live_available reflects whether the deployment has an OPENROUTER_API_KEY configured, which this demo lane doesn't need -- every module call below is sent with live:false-by-default and api/run.py itself falls back to the offline lane gracefully even if live:true is requested without a key. Gating on live_available would fail a perfectly healthy, correctly-running demo deployment. live_available is still surfaced in the final response (see 'Merge Module Summaries') for a reviewer's visibility. The false branch below is reachable now (api/run.py's build_get_response() previously hardcoded ok:true unconditionally, which made this a dead branch even under REPO_ROOT_ERROR -- fixed: ok is now repo_root_ok, i.e. real deployment health, not a constant). See the new repo_root_ok / error fields on this same response for the detail behind a false.

nodes.name: Engine API Unreachable
nodes.notes: Fed from both the health-check's error output (transport failure) and the ok:false branch (service up but reporting a problem, e.g. REPO_ROOT_ERROR from a bad deployment). Either way the failure is legible here instead of the workflow hanging on a Wait node the way the production lane's first version did.

nodes.name: M1 — Enrichment
nodes.notes: Generic HTTP: engine's public API has no native n8n node. Summary keys per api/run.py summarize_m1(): input_rows, output_rows, duplicates_merged, excluded_rows, contact_completeness_pct, company_completeness_pct, tier1/2/3, llm_calls_made, llm_rows_patched. This request always sends live:false-by-default (see jsonBody) for this demo lane, so the top-level 'lane' field on the response is always 'offline' here -- api/run.py's live/degraded distinction (lane:'live' vs lane:'degraded' when a --live request silently fell back to the rule table) only applies when a caller sets live:true, which the production lane (master.json) exercises, not this demo lane. onError=continueErrorOutput catches transport-level failure only -- a graceful API-level failure (HTTP 200, body ok:false) lands on THIS node's success output instead and is caught later in 'Merge Module Summaries', since api/run.py always answers 200.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ { "module": "m1", "live": $('Build Run Request').item.json.live, "event_name": $('Build Run Request').item.json.event_name, "registrants_csv": $('Build Run Request').item.json.base_request.registrants_csv, "transcript_md": $('Build Run Request').item.json.base_request.transcript_md } }}

nodes.name: Completeness ≥ 90%? (SDR-handoff bar)
nodes.notes: Expresses the brief's own acceptance bar (contact_completeness_pct >= 90) as a workflow branch, not just a number buried in a report. Both branches reconverge on M2 -- this flags a below-bar run for a reviewer without dead-ending the demo (the workflow's whole point is to complete green end to end). Guarded: M1's success output also carries a graceful {ok:false} body (HTTP 200, no summary key -- see 'M1 — Enrichment' node's notes), and reading .contact_completeness_pct off a missing summary would throw and red out the whole execution. The expression below falls back to -1 (always < 90) in that case, so an M1-level failure routes to the same below-bar branch instead of crashing the node -- 'Flag: Below SDR-Handoff Bar' downstream is guarded the same way and reports the real error/hint text when summary is missing.

nodes.name: Flag: Below SDR-Handoff Bar
nodes.notes: Purely a visual/log flag for this execution path -- the actual pass/fail number the final response reports is recomputed independently from M1's own summary in 'Merge Module Summaries', so this branch never needs to be read back downstream. Guarded the same way as the IF node upstream: reads $json.error/.hint instead of $json.summary.contact_completeness_pct when M1 returned a graceful {ok:false} (no summary key), so an M1 failure produces a legible flag message instead of throwing here.

assignments.name: handoff_flag
assignments.value: ={{ $json.summary ? ('below 90% SDR-handoff bar: ' + $json.summary.contact_completeness_pct + '% contact completeness (see M1 summary in the final response)') : ('m1 reported ok:false -- ' + ($json.error || 'unknown error') + ' (see hint in the final response)') }}

nodes.name: M2 — Comms
nodes.notes: Generic HTTP, same engine API. Summary keys: segments, recipients, subject_variants, utm_campaign, approval_status. Independent call (doesn't consume M1's output body -- api/run.py reruns its own inputs per module), sequenced here so the canvas reads like the real M1->M2->M3->M4 pipeline.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ { "module": "m2", "live": $('Build Run Request').item.json.live, "event_name": $('Build Run Request').item.json.event_name, "registrants_csv": $('Build Run Request').item.json.base_request.registrants_csv, "transcript_md": $('Build Run Request').item.json.base_request.transcript_md } }}

nodes.name: M3 — Repurpose
nodes.notes: Generic HTTP, same engine API. Summary keys: blog_words, social_posts, youtube_chapters, assets, blog_within_spec, social_within_spec.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ { "module": "m3", "live": $('Build Run Request').item.json.live, "event_name": $('Build Run Request').item.json.event_name, "registrants_csv": $('Build Run Request').item.json.base_request.registrants_csv, "transcript_md": $('Build Run Request').item.json.base_request.transcript_md } }}

nodes.name: M4 — Dashboard
nodes.notes: Generic HTTP, same engine API. Summary keys: registrants, attendees, mql, attendee_to_mql_pct, top_accounts, committee_accounts, anomalies, narrative_source. api/run.py reruns M1 offline internally to feed M4 (M4 has no --live flag -- pure computation), so this call is self-sufficient even though it comes after M1-M3 in the visual pipeline.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ { "module": "m4", "live": $('Build Run Request').item.json.live, "event_name": $('Build Run Request').item.json.event_name, "registrants_csv": $('Build Run Request').item.json.base_request.registrants_csv, "transcript_md": $('Build Run Request').item.json.base_request.transcript_md } }}

nodes.name: Shape Module Error
nodes.notes: Shared handler for all four module HTTP nodes' error outputs (transport-level failures only -- network error, timeout, non-2xx; api/run.py's own graceful ok:false failures land on the SUCCESS output instead and are caught in 'Merge Module Summaries'). $prevNode.name identifies which of the four calls actually failed, since only one of the four connections into this node fires per execution.

nodes.name: Respond: Module Error
nodes.notes: Returns the shaped error as the webhook response (HTTP 200 with ok:false, matching api/run.py's own convention of never hard-failing the transport). No-op when this execution was started by Manual Trigger (no webhook to respond to).

nodes.name: Merge Module Summaries
nodes.notes: Collects all four module responses by referencing each HTTP node by name (safe here: this node only runs once all four have succeeded at the transport level). Also catches the API-level ok:false case that 'Shape Module Error' can't see (api/run.py always answers HTTP 200, so a module-internal failure is a normal success output with ok:false in the body, not a node error) -- overall ok is false if any module reports ok:false, even though the n8n execution itself is still green. run_key/event_name come from 'Derive Run Key'; engine_live_available comes from the health-check response.

nodes.name: Respond: Success
nodes.notes: Returns the merged 4-module result as the webhook response. No-op when this execution was started by Manual Trigger.

nodes.name: Shape Run Summary (execution log)
nodes.notes: Terminal node, not wired to the webhook response -- exists so a reviewer scanning the n8n execution list (Executions tab) sees a compact one-line summary per run without opening the full merged JSON.

parameters.content:
## CLOUD DEMO LANE — zero credentials
Runs green end to end on a completely fresh n8n Cloud instance. Every external call in this workflow goes to the engine's own public, keyless API:

`POST https://postevent-engine.vercel.app/api/run` `{module, live, ...}`

Trigger it either way:
- Click **Execute Workflow** (Manual Trigger)
- `curl` the Webhook's test/production URL, path `postevent-demo`

No HubSpot / Clay / Telegram credentials anywhere in this file. For the real CRM-writing lane, see `master.json` (production lane) and its own sticky note.

## ERROR BRANCH
Catches transport-level failures only (network error / timeout / non-2xx) from any of the four module calls — retryOnFail already tried 2-3x first. `Shape Module Error` identifies which call failed via `$prevNode.name` and shapes a `{ok:false, module, error, hint}` body; `Respond: Module Error` returns it as the webhook response (HTTP 200, matching api/run.py's own never-hard-fail convention).

A *graceful* API-level failure (HTTP 200, body `ok:false` — e.g. a broken deployment) does **not** land here; it flows through each HTTP node's normal success output and is caught in `Merge Module Summaries` instead.

## WANT THE REAL CRM WRITES?
This lane only calls the engine's read-only /api/run — it never touches HubSpot, Clay, or Telegram, so it can't demonstrate the actual downstream GTM writes.

See `orchestrator/n8n/cloud/master.json` ("Post-Event Engine — Cloud Production") for the real HubSpot batch-upsert / associate / send lane, and this repo's README for exactly which nodes there need credentials wired before it will run.
